question: Is label-blind scanner-code grain/noise amplitude repeat-stable across fixed crops, independent scans and a frozen development/confirmation split strongly enough to justify a later generic amplitude-fit experiment?

estimator.input: native scanner RGB code normalized by fixed-crop mean
estimator.detrend: same fixed least-squares quadratic as P4R
estimator.amplitude: 1.4826 times median absolute deviation from the residual median
estimator.crop_amplitude: median of three RGB channel amplitudes
estimator.scan_amplitude: median of four preregistered crop amplitudes

branch_rule.pass: retain scanner-code amplitude as a generic same-scanner development/confirmation target and open one separately frozen global-amplitude candidate fit
branch_rule.fail: close amplitude fitting from this source; keep only normalized NPS/ACF shape evidence and do not resume photographic material integration

claim_ceiling: Same-scanner label-blind relative code-amplitude feasibility; not optical density, emulsion grain amplitude, stock/process/scanner-independent calibration or product evidence.
